[{"node": "menu_content111", "element": "menu_content", "data": {"label": "Combos", "key": "combos_menu_content", "id": "combos_menu_content", "name": "combos_menu_content"}, "elements": [{"node": "markdown101", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Options, sizes and combos", "key": "md_options_sizes_and_combos", "id": "options-sizes-and-combos", "name": "md_options_sizes_and_combos", "value": "# Options, sizes and combos

Everything a guest can choose is set on the **Item** itself, in its **Restaurant** tab, with three ideas:

| What changes | How it's set up | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **What the product is** (price, stock or recipe change) | ERPNext **Item Variants** | Fries Small / Large, Soda Small / Medium / Large |
| **What it is made of** | **Components**: other items, *Included* or *Optional* | NO Tomato, Cheese x2, Onion Rings instead of Fries |
| **How to prepare it** (nothing changes in stock) | **Instructions**: options without a component | Medium rare, No salt, No ice |

When a server adds the item, a picker opens already set the way the item comes; they only change what the guest asks for, like in a delivery app.
"}}, {"node": "markdown102", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Components", "key": "md_components", "id": "components", "name": "md_components", "value": "# Components

Each row of **Options** is one option:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Section | Groups the options: *Burger*, *Side*, *Drink*, *Cooking*… Empty = **Ingredients** |
| Role | **Included**: comes with the item, starts checked, can be removed (**NO Tomato**). **Optional**: can be added or chosen |
| Component | The item it is: an ingredient, a side, a drink, another dish. Empty = an instruction for the kitchen |
| Label | What the server sees. Empty = the component's name |
| Price | Optional: what it adds. Included: what it's worth (taken off when removed) |
| Changes the price | Off: choosing or removing it never changes the price |
| Up to | How many times it can be chosen (*Cheese x2*) |
| Portion | How much of the component goes in one unit (30 g of tomato) |
| Preselected | An optional row that comes checked (the usual cooking point) |
| Default variant | For a component with sizes: the one included |
| Unavailable | 86 the option without touching the item |

Because components are items, they bring their own choices one level down: a **Classic Burger** inside a combo offers its parts and cooking point; a **Fountain Soda** asks for its size. The kitchen reads **Classic Burger: NO Tomato, Medium** and **Fountain Soda: Large, No ice**.

Included parts left as they come are not printed, so tickets only show what changed.
"}}, {"node": "markdown103", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Sections and Option Lists", "key": "md_sections_and_option_lists", "id": "sections-and-option-lists", "name": "md_sections_and_option_lists", "value": "# Sections and Option Lists

The **Sections** table sets the rules of each section:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Minimum choices | 0 = optional, 1 or more = required |
| Maximum choices | 1 = pick one, 0 = no limit |
| Free choices | The first N optional ones are free, the cheapest first (2 free sauces) |
| Ingredient modes | Each chosen option offers the restaurant's modes: Light, Extra, On the side… |
| Option List | Shared options offered in this section |

An **Option List** holds options shared by many items: *Cooking Point*, *Sauces*, *Sides*. Create it once with its rules and add it to a section of each item; editing the list changes every item that uses it.

Sections appear in the order of the Sections table; a section not listed there goes where its options are.
"}}, {"node": "markdown104", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Sizes are variants", "key": "md_sizes_are_variants", "id": "sizes-are-variants", "name": "md_sizes_are_variants", "value": "# Sizes are variants

A size that changes the price, the stock or the recipe is an ERPNext **Item Variant**:

1. Create the item (e.g. *Fries*) with **Has Variants** and the attribute **Size**.
2. Create its variants (*Fries-S*, *Fries-L*), each with its **Item Price** and, if it has one, its own recipe: the large one can use 250 g of potatoes instead of 150 g.
3. Put the template on the menu. Set the options on the template: every variant uses them.

The POS shows the template once, **from $3.49**, and asks for the size; the line is the variant (**Fries Large**). Inside a combo, a component with sizes includes its **default variant** (or the cheapest) and bigger ones charge the difference.

A size that only changes the price, without changing stock or recipe, can simply be an option with a price.
"}}, {"node": "markdown105", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Option prices by size", "key": "md_option_prices_by_size", "id": "option-prices-by-size", "name": "md_option_prices_by_size", "value": "# Option prices by size

Toppings usually cost more on a large pizza. Mark the section **Price by size** and give each size an **Option price factor** (in the variant's Restaurant tab):

| Size | Pizza | Factor | Pepperoni ($2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small | $10.99 | 1 | $2.00 |
| Large | $14.99 | 1.5 | $3.00 |

Sections not marked keep their prices (a dip costs the same on any size). Changing the size in the picker keeps what was chosen and updates the prices.
"}}, {"node": "markdown106", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Combos made in several stations", "key": "md_combos_made_in_several_stations", "id": "combos-made-in-several-stations", "name": "md_combos_made_in_several_stations", "value": "# Combos made in several stations

Turn on **Send components to their stations** in a combo's Restaurant tab. Each component that is a menu item goes to the production center of its own item group, with its own status:

- the **Classic Burger** to the grill, with its changes (*NO Tomato, Medium*);
- the **Fries Small** to the fryer;
- the **Cappuccino** to the coffee bar.

The waiter still sees one line, one price and one invoice. The combo stays *Sent* until its last part is ready; then it takes that status, so a center that handles combos as a whole (an expo) gets it complete. Ingredients and instructions of the combo itself are not split.
"}}, {"node": "markdown107", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "How the price works", "key": "md_how_the_price_works", "id": "how-the-price-works", "name": "md_how_the_price_works", "value": "# How the price works

Each item chooses its pricing in its **Restaurant** tab:

**Fixed price** (default): the item's own price, then:

- an optional component adds its price for each unit chosen;
- removing an included part takes its price off;
- more units of an included part add the extra units;
- a bigger size of a component adds the difference;
- options with *Changes the price* off never change it.

**Price from Components**: the item's price is the sum of what is chosen (build-your-own bowls, pizzas by topping). The catalog shows the price of what comes checked.

The price is never below zero, and it is always computed by the server; the picker shows it live.
"}}, {"node": "markdown108", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Ingredient modes", "key": "md_ingredient_modes", "id": "ingredient-modes", "name": "md_ingredient_modes", "value": "# Ingredient modes

Each restaurant defines its **Modifier Modes**; Light, Extra and On the side come installed:

| Mode | Kitchen text | Price | Portion |
|---|---|---|---|
| Light | LIGHT {0} | free | half |
| Extra | EXTRA {0} | the option's price once more | double |
| On the side | {0} ON THE SIDE | free | the same |

Edit them or add your own (with a restaurant, or empty for all). In a section with **Ingredient modes**, every checked option shows *Normal* and the modes as buttons; unchecking it is always **NO**. The portion matters for recipes: *Light tomato* takes out half the tomato.
"}}, {"node": "markdown109", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Swaps", "key": "md_swaps", "id": "swaps", "name": "md_swaps", "value": "# Swaps

In a pick-one section, make the usual side **Included** and the others **Optional**. Choosing onion rings instead of fries prints **Onion Rings (instead of Fries)** and charges the difference.
"}}, {"node": "markdown110", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Example: a burger combo", "key": "md_example_a_burger_combo", "id": "example-a-burger-combo", "name": "md_example_a_burger_combo", "value": "# Example: a burger combo

*Classic Burger Combo*, fixed price **$12.99**, no recipe of its own:

| Section (rules) | Component | Role | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| Burger | Classic Burger (its own parts, cooking point, sauces) | Included | 0 |
| Side (pick 1) | Fries (sizes Small / Large) | Included | 0 |
| | Onion Rings | Optional | 1.50 |
| | Coleslaw | Optional | 0 |
| Drink (pick 1) | Fountain Soda (Small / Medium / Large) | Included | 0 |
| | Sparkling Water | Optional | 0.50 |

The guest asks for no tomato, onion rings and a large soda without ice:

`12.99 + 1.50 (onion rings) + 1.00 (Large instead of Small) = $15.49`

The kitchen ticket reads:

```text
1 x Classic Burger Combo
   > Classic Burger: NO Tomato, Medium
   > Onion Rings (instead of Fries)
   > Fountain Soda: Large, No ice
```

Stock: the burger's recipe without the tomato leaves stock; the fries don't.
